**1. Entity-index backfill: one `entire graph diff` spawn per commit** — `internal/entityindex/build.go:721` → `graphdiff.go:102`. A full backfill walks up to 20,000 commits (`maxWalkCommits`), spawning the provider CLI for each. This is partly a recorded decision: Brain facts show the work was deliberately moved to a detached backfill after synchronous runs blew the hook budget, and batching spawns was rejected because it needs a cross-binary contract change, "revisit if spawn overhead becomes material." The real fix would be a provider range-diff API (one spawn emits per-commit deltas from a warm index).

**2. Hosted pull filter: one `git merge-base --is-ancestor` per distinct anchor commit** — `internal/cli/hosted_pull_filter.go:26`. Memoized, but the server ships the whole repo feed, so a pull can shell out once per distinct teammate commit — while holding the brain write lock (the code's own comment flags this). A single `git rev-list HEAD` loaded into a set answers every reachability question with one spawn.

**3. Semantic overlay refresh: `git rev-parse` per local branch** — `internal/cli/refresh.go:987`. The branch list already comes from one `for-each-ref` at line 950; adding `%(objectname)` to its format deletes the whole loop of spawns. This repo has 101 local branches, so that's ~100 execs per refresh. Cheapest fix of the set.
